$comment: WORKED EXAMPLE 2 of 2 (org-overlay lane). An org extends the core catalogue with a private invariant about its own staging database. private=true: the loader strips this entry from every public artifact (privacy property, unit-tested). Values are synthetic. This file lives in examples/ as documentation; a REAL org overlay belongs in the gitignored catalogue-contrib/org-overlays/ directory and never leaves the machine.
intent: The staging database cluster must never be dropped by an agent: the direct drop form is forbidden at the rules layer, and every spelling variant must surface as an explicit unknown, never as an allow.
name: staging_database_drop_block

parameters.description: Protected cluster DSN (synthetic; the real overlay binds the org's actual DSN)

probe_families.note: Quoted/flag-variant spellings do not match the literal bound form.

provenance.detail: Example Org internal policy POL-DB-07 ('no destructive operations against staging datastores without DBA approval'), rev 3. Org-private provenance.

rationale: Staging shares the production schema and seed data; a drop costs a full day of engineer time to rebuild and has happened twice via automation.
severity_rationale: No customer data at risk (staging), but rebuild cost and incident history justify a hard block.
